panels.rationale: Single ultrasound panel of right axillary supernumerary breast in 39-year-old woman showing circumscribed homogeneous solid mass, directly supporting ectopic breast tissue on ultrasound for accessory_breast_tissue.
panels.attribution_text: Conde et al. Fibroadenoma in axillary supernumerary breast: case report.. Sao Paulo medical journal = Revista paulista de medicina 2005. doi:10.1590/s1516-31802005000500011. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: ght axillary breast exhibited a round, partially circumscribed mass, measuring 1.1 cm in diameter (Figure 1). Ultrasonography of the accessory breasts performed in November 2002 had revealed a 1.1 cm mass in the right axilla. A new ultrasound scan was performed, which demonstrated no abnormality in the left axillary breast, but showed a clearly circumscribed, homogeneous solid mass, measuring 1.1 cm in diameter in the right axilla (Figure 2), thus maintaining the same characteristics as seen previously. No biopsy or cytological study of the mass was performed. Renal ultrasonography was normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: HE histology from left supernumerary breast specimen showing ectopic mammary ducts/lobules with low-grade DCIS and microcalcifications; article title confirms supernumerary breast DCIS case. B: ER immunohistochemistry of same left supernumerary breast specimen showing ectopic mammary epithelium with ER positivity, supporting accessory breast tissue origin.
panels.attribution_text: Bui et al. Management of Low-Grade Ductal Carcinoma In Situ in a Supernumerary Breast: A Case Report.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.94169. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology (A) 40x magnification images of a hematoxylin & eosin (HE) section from a left supernumerary breast specimen. Slide is from a cystic space lined with papillary projections, with microscopy demonstrating multiple nests of tumor cells with nuclear pleomorphism (red arrow) and loss of nuclear polarity, along with some microcalcifications (blue arrow). (B) Cells stained positively for estrogen receptor.
in_text_mentions: tified intraductal papilloma without evidence of atypia or malignancy. After biopsy, the mass decreased in size, but the patient noted regrowth 4 months later. After extensive discussion with the patient, an excisional biopsy was performed, and histopathology revealed low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with microcalcifications measuring at least 5 mm (Figure 3). All margins were negative, with the distance to the closest margin measuring 1 mm. The immunohistochemistry study showed positive estrogen (97%) and progesterone (94%) receptors. A screening mammogram at this time was benign BI-RADS 2.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Panel a is diagnostic ultrasound of supernumerary nipple site on upper abdomen in article about supernumerary nipples, showing hypoechoic well-defined mass in relation to nipple, corresponding to ectopic breast tissue on ultrasound. b: Panel b is ultrasound-guided biopsy of same tumour at supernumerary nipple site, still showing ectopic tissue mass on ultrasound; procedural image but diagnostic, not treatment exclusion.
panels.attribution_text: Öwall et al. Syringomatous Tumour Presenting as Inversion of a Supernumerary Nipple.. Case reports in pathology 2019. doi:10.1155/2019/9461815. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound of upper abdominal wall right side (a). Ultrasound guided needle core biopsy (16G) of the tumour located on the upper abdominal wall right side (b).
in_text_mentions: A 61-year-old woman presented with two supernumerary nipples located along the milk line on each side of the upper abdomen. During a few months before referral, the patient had noticed a firm palpable mass in close relations to the supernumerary nipple on the right side (Figure 1). She had no other symptoms. Bilateral mammogram and ultrasound revealed normal breast parenchyma.
